notes: Version 3.7 corrects the section on the projection structure. The statement that admissible injective projections have trivial holonomy, previously adopted as a reading not proved here, is now cited from the white paper (Appendix A.9, Theorem A.1 and Corollary A.1) in its exact scope: for an admissible projection in the white paper's sense, a smooth fibre-bundle map supporting a connection, injectivity makes every fibre a single point, so that in the principal case the structure group and the holonomy group are trivial and the fibre connection is flat. The paper states that it does not establish that its projection satisfies these hypotheses. The sentences that drew from this a conclusion on the curvature of the effective geometry are removed; the necessity of a non-injective projection is now attributed to the no-go theorem of the ENI paper alone. A footnote corrects the provenance of the finite-q values of the admissibility weight quoted in versions 2.3.1 to 3.4 and withdrawn in version 3.5: they come from the simulation code published with Q5a and a rerun of that code with its committed parameter tables reproduces them; on pairs whose admissible basis has full rank their modulation terms equal 2 exactly, because every entry of a fingerprint vector has the same modulus, their shift terms are only numerically close to 2 on average, and they do not bear on Hypothesis [H-w], which remains open. All theorems and results of the paper are unchanged.
